newsitem.title: QATAR: Enron, Qatar to begin "crucial" talks next week.
newsitem.headline: Enron, Qatar to begin "crucial" talks next week.

text.p: Qatar and Enron Corp of the United States are to begin a "crucial" round of talks next week to put a $4 billion liquefied natural gas (LNG) deal in place, an industry source said on Tuesday.

"A 10-member Enron team will arrive in Doha on Friday and spend about 10 days from Saturday to finalise various aspects of the deal," said a source close to Qatar Enron LNG Marketing Co, which is spearheading the project.
"It is going to be a crucial meeting."
Qatar has given Enron approval to market five million tonnes of LNG annually from 2001 from the planned joint venture.

In October 1995 Enron and Israel signed a memorandum of understanding granting the Houston-based company 180 days to finalise an agreement for the supply of at least two million tonnes a year of Qatari gas. The agreement gave Enron exclusivity in negotiations with Qatar during this period.
An Israeli official's statement last week that Enron no longer had an exclusive agreement to negotiate with Qatar for LNG supplies to Israel had triggered doubts about the project.

But the industry source told Reuters: "The project is very much on course and they hope to see an agreement soon to set up a joint venture formally by year-end...The final go-ahead is expected by the year-end, financing by 1998 and production of LNG by 2001."

The source said the sides would discuss the shareholding structure for the joint venture, a production sharing agreement related to the financing and development of the North Field tract and issues relating to sales and purchase agreements.
Qatar possesses around 530 trillion cubic feet of natural gas in its continental shelf, known as the North Field.
He said according to a letter of intent signed by Qatar and Enron in January 1995, state-owned Qatar General Petroleum Co (QGPC) would hold 60 percent and Enron would hold 40 percent.
"Now QGPC is looking for a revised shareholding of 65 percent for itself and 35 percent for Enron," the source said.
He said India would be an important market for Enron.
"They are looking for two more buyers in India -- Oil India Ltd and Essar Group -- to have the customer base in place," he said.
The U.S. company is also building a $2.8 billion power plant in the western Indian port city of Dabhol, where it needs at least two million tonnes of gas a year.

The meetings will be the second round of Qatar-Enron talks this month. Last week Enron Development Corp chairman and chief executive officer Rebecca Mark visited Qatar and met the emir, Sheikh Hamad bin Khalifa al-Thani, and the Minister of Energy and Industry Abdullah bin Hamad al-Attiyah.
